observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon AF-S NIKKOR lens with visible text “AF-S NIKKOR” and “50mm 1/8G” (likely 50mm f/1.8G) on the front ring.
Photo 1 shows the side label area with “Nikon” and “AF-S NIKKOR” and the front glass; no obvious cracks are visible.
Photo 2 shows the front element and the front ring text “Nikon” and “50mm 1/8G” (again likely f/1.8G).
The seller’s claim says “American used lens”, but the photos only show a Nikon lens; no country-of-origin marking is clearly readable.

identity.model: AF-S NIKKOR 50mm f/1.8G (read as “50mm 1/8G” on the lens in photos 0/1/2)

claims.evidence: Photos show a Nikon lens but no clearly readable country-of-origin/market marking.
Photos show the front element, but there’s no close-up of the glass for haze/fungus/scratches and no back-element view.

risks.risk: Fungus/haze/scratches on the front or rear element not clearly visible in these angles
risks.proof: One clear close-up photo of the front element under light + one close-up of the rear element (through the mount) + a short video of the lens tilted to show reflections.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed clean (worst case: assume minor haze/scratches possible).

risks.risk: Autofocus may be weak or not working (common issue on used lenses) even if it looks fine
risks.proof: Video of autofocus hunting and then locking on a nearby subject using a camera body (show focus confirmation/AF indicator).

risks.risk: Aperture blades may be sticky or aperture may not respond correctly
risks.proof: Photo/video showing aperture changes (e.g., set f/1.8 then f/4 then f/8 on camera and show exposure change) or a test shot series.

risks.risk: Mount damage or loose fit (could cause wobble or poor connection)
risks.proof: Close-up of the lens mount contacts and bayonet from straight-on, plus a photo showing it seated firmly on a camera body.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as mount condition not guaranteed.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (front/rear caps, hood) affecting value
risks.proof: Photo showing everything included laid out (front cap, rear cap, hood if any, pouch/box).

proof_requests: Close-up of front element and rear element (through mount) in sharp focus under bright light
Short autofocus test video on a camera body (show it locking)
Aperture test: set different f-stops on camera and show exposure change or a small test shot series
Clear photo of mount/bayonet and contacts; show lens seated on camera
List and photo of included items (front cap/rear cap/hood/box)
response.reason: The lens identity (Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 50mm f/1.8G) is readable from the photos, but “clean like new” and functional condition (AF/aperture) are not verifiable remotely from these images. To price confidently, you need element close-ups and a basic camera test.
